candidate_findings.title: Analytics lacks a deterministic and truthful scan-state contract
candidate_findings.claim: The bounded excerpt mixes sequence-ordered replay, sliding time windows, and either sequence or timestamp checkpoints without defining event-time cutoffs, expired-event eviction, late-event handling, overlap, crash atomicity, or scan failure/cancellation state. Previously written rollups can therefore remain visible or be overwritten without a deterministic freshness oracle.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Retries, crashes, delayed events, and simultaneous periodic/on-demand scans can miss, double-count, retain expired usage, or regress the dashboard while the GUI continues presenting an old rollup.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require a single canonical sequence watermark plus explicit event-time semantics, window eviction/recomputation rules, atomic rollup-and-checkpoint commit, single-flight or generation ordering, and persisted running/succeeded/failed/cancelled/stale metadata with last-success sequence and time.

evidence_refs.excerpt: sequence order, not file mtime, is the source of truth for replay ordering
On-demand refresh should leave the previously written rollups visible until the new scan completes.
Last N hours (e.g. at least 7d for `tool_usage.7d`) or since last scan checkpoint.
Store "last scanned up to seq X" or "last scanned timestamp" in redb

candidate_findings.title: The canonical 24h analytics window has no computation or checklist contract
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt declares `24h` canonical for MVP, but both the computation prose and implementation checklist specify only 5h/7d usage aggregation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can legitimately omit or inconsistently derive the 24h rollup, leaving consumers and tests without a deterministic expected key or value.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the 24h input events, cutoff semantics, output key/meta key, aggregation formula, refresh behavior, and acceptance oracle alongside 5h and 7d.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Canonical tool-usage windows for MVP are `5h`, `24h`, and `7d`; `1h` remains optional.
For 5h/7d: aggregate `usage.event` by platform
compute 5h/7d, tool latency, and **tool_usage**

candidate_findings.title: Missing background worktree fields silently select the main project
candidate_findings.claim: Consumers are told to interpret absent optional worktree fields as main-project context, but the excerpt provides no rule that validates the thread was unbound at enqueue time or rejects an incomplete bound-thread event.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A producer bug, schema downgrade, or partial event can redirect background mutation from an intended worktree into the main checkout without surfacing ambiguity.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Freeze `thread_id`, `effective_project_id`, binding generation, `worktree_id`, path, branch, and HEAD at enqueue; permit absence only after an authoritative unbound check; reject or quarantine records inconsistent with the binding projection rather than defaulting ambiguity to main.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Consumers treat absent fields as main-project context rather than inventing worktree context.

candidate_findings.title: Worktree operation events cannot reliably correlate retries or concurrent attempts
candidate_findings.claim: Merge, PR, and pre-merge-test minimum payloads lack a required operation/attempt/idempotency identifier; test terminal events also lack a required causal reference to the started event, and no cancelled terminal event is defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Repeated identical commands or concurrent attempts on one thread/worktree cannot be paired deterministically, so replay may attach a pass/failure to the wrong attempt or duplicate a merge/PR side effect.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Add a required operation/attempt ID, causal parent/start reference, idempotency key, generation or expected HEAD, exact terminal exclusivity, and explicit cancelled/aborted outcomes for every side-effecting lifecycle.

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Permission checks, routing, billing attribution, history, and audit consumers can select different account identities for the same attempt.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide one typed runtime-identity schema defining required versus optional fields, stable-key relationships, provider/account pair structure, precedence on disagreement, credential-reference constraints, and compatibility migration from every alias.

candidate_findings.title: Question item and questionnaire lifecycle states are conflated
candidate_findings.claim: One paragraph calls five values canonical statuses while the next introduces another set containing both `draft` and `/draft`, plus `paused`, without assigning states to item versus session or defining legal transitions and terminality.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Reload, timeout, resend, and concurrent submit paths can reconstruct contradictory cards or resubmit an already terminal answer.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Separate item-answer status from questionnaire-session status; remove or normalize `/draft`; define initial, terminal, and legal transitions, timeout authority, submit/resend idempotency, active-run linkage, and conflict resolution.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Canonical status values are `answered | submitted | dismissed | timed_out | unavailable`

candidate_findings.title: TODO mutation payload cannot enforce the promised revision model
candidate_findings.claim: The plan requires bounded revisions and new revision events after execution begins, but its minimal mutation payload contains no revision ID, expected version, transaction/batch ID, thread/run scope, or idempotency key.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent user/agent edits and multi-item reorder operations can interleave, lose updates, or replay into a normalized TODO list that never corresponded to an approved revision.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define plan revision identity and parent revision, optimistic preconditions, atomic batches for add/remove/reorder, operation idempotency, thread/run scope, ordering semantics, and deterministic rejection/rebase behavior.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Plan/TODO persistence is locked to explicit revision states, structural-edit gating after approval, bounded revision history
minimal payload schema `{ plan_id: string, todo_id: string, field: string, old_value: any, new_value: any, source: "agent" | "user" }`
After execution begins, reorder or status corrections create a new TODO revision event instead of mutating the approved plan in place.

candidate_findings.title: Progress and cancellation payloads lack ordering and terminal-state rules
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt requires reconstructible progress and a `cancelled: true` terminal state but does not define a progress sequence, phase enum, monotonic-count rules, completion-versus-cancellation precedence, late-event handling, or finality of partial results.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent or delayed events can make chat, GUI, replay, and audit disagree about whether an operation completed, was cancelled, or has usable partial output.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define operation/attempt anchoring, monotonically increasing progress sequence, legal phases, terminal outcome enum and exclusivity, cancellation acknowledgement, late-event rejection, partial-result status, and replay test vectors.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Long-running activity transparency persists `progress_event` payloads so chat, GUI, replay, and audit views can reconstruct operation phase, detail text, completed/total counts, elapsed timing, estimated remaining time, cancellation, and partial-result state
Long-running progress payloads persist `cancelled: true` when cancellation is the terminal state

candidate_findings.title: Sensitive command and web content is persisted without a data-handling boundary
candidate_findings.claim: The bounded excerpt mandates durable command blocks and full web page/research/source payloads but states no redaction, credential detection, encryption, access control, export filtering, retention, deletion propagation, or audit-view authorization rules for that content.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal commands, URLs, page bodies, and source sets can contain tokens, filesystem identities, private prompts, or regulated data that then leaks through history, export, replay, or audit surfaces.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define field-level data classification, secret scrubbing before persistence, encrypted storage, viewer/export permissions, retention and legal-hold behavior, deletion/GC propagation, and safe handling of opaque blobs and previews.

candidate_findings.title: Reload re-executes persisted visualizer code without a frozen runtime contract
candidate_findings.claim: PM persists HTML/JS/CSS and re-renders it on reload/export, while version/integrity requirements are stated only for bundled scripts or third-party refs. The excerpt omits renderer/runtime versioning, policy revalidation, revoked dependency behavior, network and resource limits, timeouts, and a deterministic fallback rule.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The same stored thread can render differently after upgrades or re-execute code that is newly unsafe, unavailable, or unbounded, compromising deterministic history and client safety.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist renderer/sandbox/CSP versions and dependency hashes; revalidate policy on replay; define quarantine and revoked-library behavior, network/CPU/memory/time limits, deterministic output oracle, and exact screenshot-fallback conditions with a visible provenance state.

candidate_findings.title: The unsaved-editor record is under-keyed and does not specify durable edit content
candidate_findings.claim: Recovery snapshots must include host/path identity and local buffer state, but the key contains only project plus path hash and the listed stored fields omit the dirty text/delta or a durable content reference and base-content digest.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Local and remote resources can collide or restore into the wrong host/path, and after a crash the record may prove a buffer was dirty without containing enough data to reconstruct the edits or detect the exact base-version conflict.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Include canonical host/resource identity and collision handling in the key; persist crash-atomic encrypted content or deltas plus base digest/version, encoding and line-ending metadata; define snapshot cadence, corruption recovery, partial restore, retention, and deterministic conflict tests.

evidence_refs.excerpt: recovery snapshots store local buffer state, capture metadata, host/path identity, and write availability at capture time

stores: cursor position, scroll offset, selection ranges, undo stack reference, and unsaved changes flag

candidate_findings.title: Requested/effective projection state omits required health and write-availability contracts
candidate_findings.claim: The section requires freshness, health, and write availability to remain distinguishable, but implements only a three-value freshness enum. `current` means merely "just resolved" with no timestamp, watermark, expiry, authority, restart rule, or health/write enum.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A projection can remain labeled current after its remote source becomes unhealthy or read-only, misleading users and downstream mutation gates after restart.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define independent typed freshness, health, and write-availability fields; authoritative resolver and timestamps/watermarks; legal transitions and crash recovery; stale/refresh timeout; mutation gating; and cross-surface display/test oracles.

evidence_refs.excerpt:
- freshness vs health vs write availability for remote-backed projections
- restore outcome for historical Search, LSP, browser, and editor recovery surfaces

- projection freshness is persisted as `current`, `refreshing`, or `stale`
- `current` means just resolved, `refreshing` means re-resolution is in progress, and `stale` means the projection needs refresh before it should be treated as current

candidate_findings.title: Source Control projection is scoped only by project despite worktree-specific state
candidate_findings.claim: The excerpt models worktrees by project and worktree ID, but `sc_projection.v1` is keyed only by project while storing branch, diff, staged files, compare targets, and commit draft.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Multiple repositories or worktrees in one project can overwrite each other's Source Control state, expose the wrong staged set or draft, and route review/conflict commands against the wrong checkout.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Key Source Control state by project plus repository and worktree identity; freeze HEAD/repo generation; define project-level aggregation separately; reject ambiguous commands; and specify migration from the project-only key.

evidence_refs.excerpt: `worktree_projection.v1:{project_id}:{worktree_id}` remains the project/worktree projection record.

- keys: `search_projection.v1:{project_id}` and `sc_projection.v1:{project_id}`
